note.after_visit_summary: You came in feeling down and stressed after losing your job 6 weeks ago. You've been sleeping later, eating more junk food, and pulling back from activities like basketball with friends. You're worried about money and feel guilty that your wife is working extra shifts. You deny thoughts of harming yourself or others and don't use alcohol or drugs. Based on your symptoms and questionnaire scores (PHQ-9: 11, GAD-7: 10), we believe you're experiencing an adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood—a common reaction to a major life change like job loss. The good news is this often improves with therapy. We plan to meet weekly for about an hour using cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to help you rebuild structure in your day. To start, try waking up by 7:30 a.m. on weekdays, spend two hours each morning on job searching, and call one basketball friend this week. Also, contact Tri -County HR to ask about outplacement services from your severance—this could help with job search support. If your wife Samira wants to join a session later, she’s welcome. Before you left, we reviewed a safety plan: if you ever have thoughts of hurting yourself, call or text 988 anytime. If your mood doesn’t improve with therapy, we can discuss seeing a psychiatrist, but we’ll start with therapy and see how it goes. Your next appointment is next Thursday, October 1st at 4:00 o'clock. Keep up the effort—small steps matter, and you're not alone.
